result.title: HiPPT: Physiology-Grounded Wearable PPG Representation Learning via Multi-Scope Text Alignment
result.summary: Reusable wearable PPG representations should capture local pulse morphology and broader physiological regularities. Existing pretraining objectives, however, usually apply supervision at the recording or pair level, overlooking that different concepts become reliable over different scopes of waveform evidence. We propose HiPPT, a physiology-grounded framework that matches each supervision source to its appropriate evidence scope. We construct a PPG-Text corpus of over 4 million wrist-worn recordings from 202K users, pairing recordings with waveform-derived morphology and metadata-derived context descriptions. HiPPT combines record-level morphology alignment, which grounds individual recordings in pulse characteristics, with cross-recording context alignment, which aggregates recordings sharing the same metadata tuple to capture context-consistent regularities. Waveform-guided text modeling further recovers masked contextual concepts from PPG patch representations, providing fine-grained waveform-text supervision. Across six downstream tasks spanning blood pressure, vascular stiffness, physiological attributes, and cross-dataset heart-rate estimation, HiPPT achieves the best result on the primary linear-probing metrics. The aligned space also supports zero-shot profiling of age group, sex, and BMI category, individually and jointly, with performance improving as more recordings are aggregated. These results show that evidence-scope matching yields transferable and semantically accessible wearable PPG representations. Code and pretrained weights will be released.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 HiPPT，用「证据范围匹配」的多层级文本对齐（记录级形态对齐＋跨记录上下文对齐＋波形引导文本建模）在 400 万条腕戴 PPG 数据上预训练可迁移的生理表征，并在血压、血管硬度等六项下游任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 属可穿戴生理信号的表征学习与对比对齐工作，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、latent 生成与停止决策，唯一相近点「不同概念在不同证据范围下可靠」也仅停留在波形尺度监督，缺少可供核查的 LVR 迁移线索。
